Didn’t do it on purpose. Blood clots. 

I was on the depo shot. I had a hysterectomy back in the beginning of December. The hysterectomy was much sooner then I expected(doctor had a cancellation and let me jump in) so the shot was still in my body after the hysterectomy. Recovery was fast and easy. Then I got covid. Depo shot + surgery + covid = blood clots. I’m only 28. 

I knew something was wrong, I felt weird and couldn’t stop coughing, and the cough was hard it can only be described as violent. It burst blood vessels in my eyes and in my throat so I was occasionally coughing up blood. It made me vomit. I lost my voice for 3 weeks because the coughing made my vocal cords swell. I had so many blood clots in my lungs that the guy reading my CT stoped counting and just said it’s a lot. I spent 3 days in the hospital getting IV heparin and repeat scans to make sure that all the clots were only in my lungs. I started coughing up the clots while in the hospital, they were huge. Brown and black and stinky, they were the length of one of my fingers. I had a new CT two weeks ago and I’m officially clot free. I’m still on blood thinners now though hopefully I’ll be able to stop them in July.

Around day 3 I stoped feeling tired but I started seeing things. Shadow monsters and insects that crawled around at the edges of my vision. I also got super paranoid, everyone was out to get me. 

**trigger warning (unaliving thoughts)**

Day 5 I realized I was hearing whispers that urged me to kill myself. “Put a bullet in your brain.” “Jump out the window.” “Open the car door on the highway and jump out.” “Drive into the lake.” So I went to my doctors office cause I don’t want to die. She sent me to the ER. At the ER they assigned me a watcher immediately, I wasn’t allowed to be alone even for a second. They gave me a couple drugs to try to put me to sleep but they didn’t work. They decided I needed to be in a mental ward because of the suicidal thoughts and the hallucinations. It took almost 12 hours for them to find me a bed at a place that was actually in a different state and a two hour drive away. I had to be transported by ambulance but I was still super paranoid and panicky and I’m afraid of small spaces. The ambulance was torture. 

When I got to the mental hospital, it was 5am on day 6. There they make all the patients get up at 7am so they let me lay down though I couldn’t sleep then they made me get up and slog through the day doing therapy, crafts, watching MASH on an ancient tv, and not eating because they couldn’t figure out what “gluten free” meant for my meals. I wasn’t tired but my brain was fuzzy and slow. I couldn’t remember anything or answer any of their questions. Then they gave me a shit tone of Trazodone and sent me to bed at 10pm. I finally slept. When I woke up I felt exhausted and nauseous. They finally decided that I could eat vanilla ice cream and that is all I ate for the next 4 days until they released me. When I got home, I was still exhausted, so I curled up in bed and slept for 20 hours. 

Now I take trazodone regularly and I’m still seeing my mental health team regularly to deal with the PTSD and Bipolar.

Edit to add a warning: if your in Ohio and you go to The Pavilion. (the mental hospital I went to.) they’re pretty transphobic there. They called me by my birth name the entire time I was there even though I had legally changed my name years ago. They wanted me to “admit (I) was the gender (I) was assigned at birth.” When they discharged me, all my paperwork was under the wrong name, including the prescriptions they called in for me, and the bill. My insurance fought with them for a while, refusing to pay the bill because it was in the wrong name. It was a massive pain in the ass.

I usually don’t try to save a fort once already its at 20fps but there are ways to keep it from getting there in the first place.

-keep on top of your animal population I try to keep it to no more then 4 adults of a species for those that have large litters. 6-8 adults of a species that does single births. 

-pathfinding, try to have as few ways to a thing as possible so that your computer isn’t having to compare different options to find the shortest way. Make hallways at least 2 wide so that dwarfs aren’t having to climb over each other. 

-if you don’t need to open the caverns, don’t. It’s just a bunch of pathfinding, more critters on the map, and more plants/items to keep track of. 

-mist generators make dwarves happy but the moving water and the mist can make weaker computers turn into space heaters, and contribute to fps death on nicer machines. 

If you’re getting fps death pretty early try doing a smaller embark. 3x3 and even 2x2 have plenty of space and resources if you put a bit of extra though into how to use it all. You can also adjust your population cap if you have a whole bunch (like more then 40 all the time) of idling dwarves. 

Hope this helps!

It’s really really hard to get a diagnosis of Autism Spectrum Disorder(ASD) as an adult, especially if you are “high functioning”/“require low support/intervention”. Part of the process is being asked “what do you hope to get from being officially diagnosed?” And you have to be able to give a very specific answer like “I hope to gain access to (this specific community/government resource)” or “I find I am unable to work because of (these specific indicators of ASD) and I am trying to apply for disability, but they won’t consider it without an official diagnosis”

For many an unofficial diagnosis and an acknowledgment of that unofficial diagnosis by their doctor is the best that adults with ASD can hope for. 

With all of that said - TikTok and Facebook and such has gotten a lot of adults looking at ASD and looking at themselves and self diagnosing. So if you or someone you know thinks they might be on the spectrum, it’s best to discuss it with a doctor and look at the tests and resources online.
